svg.title: Forest lost since 1990: about half the area of Europe
svg.desc: A forest at golden light. A yellow logging machine fells three trees, the forest catches fire, two Jeju roe deer run away and three white-backed woodpeckers fly off. The camera rises until the burned forest is a fiery patch on a map, beside Europe. Forest lost since 1990: 4.89 million km² (489 million hectares). Europe: about 10.2 million km². The patch slides over Europe and covers about half of it. Source: FAO, 2025. Simplified: The rise from the side view to the map is an iris: the side view zooms out inside a window shaped like the burned patch, not a true 3D camera move. Europe is a hand-simplified outline (no Novaya Zemlya, few small islands); the patch area is 48% of that outline, checked at build time.
